body:
## Summary

Formal AI's step verification does not consult the exit code of the command it ran.
The observed behaviour is consistent with keying the verdict on whether the command
produced output, which is wrong in both directions:

* a verification command that **fails** (exit 1) but prints to stdout is reported as
  **success** — the false-positive already tracked in #905;
* a verification command that **succeeds** (exit 0) but prints nothing is reported as
  **failure**, and the run is abandoned with no answer at all.

The second direction is the new report here. It is arguably worse than the first: the
work was done correctly and Formal AI threw it away.

## Reproduction — exit 0 declared a failure

`qwen` 0.21.2 against `formal-ai serve --agent-mode` (0.317.0), prompt
`Write a hello world program in Python.` Full log:
[`e2e-qwen.log`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-2130/data/runs/e2e-qwen.log)

The entire stdout of the run:

```text
The agentic CLI harness could not complete `main.py`. The tool reported:

    Command: python3 -m py_compile main.py
    Directory: (root)
    Output: (empty)
    Error: (none)
    Exit Code: 0
    Signal: 0
    Process Group PGID: 685377
```

`python3 -m py_compile` prints nothing on success — that is its documented, normal
behaviour. Formal AI chose this command itself as the verification step, then read its
correct success as a failure. Reproduced identically across two runs.

## The two directions side by side

Same server, same version, four runs:

| Log | Verification command | `Output:` | `Exit Code:` | Formal AI verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`direct-gemini3.log`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-2130/data/runs/direct-gemini3.log) | `cat hello.txt` | `exactly: Hello World` | `0` | success ✓ |
| [`direct-qwen.log`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-2130/data/runs/direct-qwen.log) | `cat hello.txt` | `cat: hello.txt: No such file or directory` | **`1`** | **success** ✗ |
| [`e2e-qwen.log`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-2130/data/runs/e2e-qwen.log) | `python3 -m py_compile main.py` | `(empty)` | **`0`** | **failure** ✗ |

The verdict tracks "was `Output:` non-empty", not the exit code. Row 2 is #905; row 3
is this issue. Both fall out of the same predicate, which is why they are worth fixing
together.

Note that in row 2 the exit code was not merely unavailable — the harness handed it
over explicitly, in the same string Formal AI quoted back verbatim in row 3.

## Suggested fix

1. **Make the exit code the primary signal.** `Exit Code: 0` is success; non-zero is
   failure. The harnesses already report it in a fixed `Exit Code: <n>` field.
2. **Never treat empty output as failure.** Silence on success is the convention for a
   large class of verification commands — `py_compile`, `tsc --noEmit`, `diff -q`,
   `test -f`, most linters. If Formal AI additionally wants content evidence, it should
   choose a command that produces some (`python3 main.py`, not `py_compile`), rather
   than reinterpreting a clean exit.
3. **Report the exit code in the failure message.** The current text — "The agentic CLI
   harness could not complete `main.py`" — attributes the failure to the harness, which
   had in fact done everything correctly.
4. As already noted in #905: treat `is_error: true` on any tool result as a step
   failure. In the row-2 run three separate `is_error: true` results were returned in a
   four-turn session and the session still terminated as `"subtype":"success"`.

## Workaround

None on the client side; the verification command and the verdict are both chosen
inside Formal AI. Callers cannot currently distinguish a real success from either
failure mode by exit code, because the process exits 0 in all of them.

## Context

Found while diagnosing link-assistant/hive-mind#2130. Companion to #905 (same
predicate, opposite direction).

Environment: formal-ai 0.317.0, qwen-code 0.21.2, gemini-cli, Linux 6.8.0, Node 24.18.1.
title: Step verification ignores the exit code: `py_compile` exiting 0 with no output is reported as a failure
